title: Constant functions are linear threshold functions
statement: For any natural number $n$, every constant Boolean function on $\{-1,1\}^n$ is a linear threshold function: there are a real threshold offset and real weights on the coordinates such that the function's value at each input is the sign of the offset plus the weighted sum of its input coordinates, with zero mapped to $1$.
hypotheses_covered: the function is the constant function with value a sign
